title: Properties of similar triangles and polygons
summary: Use equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides to solve geometric problems.
objectives: State a correct correspondence between vertices.
Form and solve proportions from corresponding sides.
Use angle sums and similarity properties together.

blocks.text: The order of vertices fixes the correspondence. If ABC is similar to PQR, then A matches P, B matches Q and C matches R. Ratios must keep that order.

A similarity statement such as triangle ABC similar to triangle PQR fixes A↔P, B↔Q and C↔R. Corresponding sides are therefore AB↔PQ, BC↔QR and AC↔PR. Mark the correspondence before forming any proportion.

Use ratios with matching orientation, such as AB/PQ=BC/QR. Cross-multiplication then solves an unknown side. Equal corresponding angles can establish AA similarity; once similarity is known, every corresponding length follows the same scale factor.

sections.title: Worked example

prompt.text: Triangles ABC and PQR are similar. AB = 8, PQ = 12, BC = 10. Find QR.

sections.verification_note: Check that every side and angle was matched in the stated corresponding order.

sections.title: Worked example: apply the method

prompt.text: Triangles ABC and PQR are similar in that order. AB=8 cm, BC=12 cm, PQ=14 cm and PR=21 cm. Find QR and AC if AC corresponds to PR.

content.text: The scale factor from ABC to PQR is PQ/AB=14/8=7/4.

sections.verification_note: The three larger-to-smaller side ratios are all 7/4.

blocks.text: Do not pair sides because they occupy a similar place on the page. Use vertex order or equal-angle markings. Avoid reversing only one ratio; write a complete correspondence line before calculating.

prompt.text: Two corresponding sides are 4 cm and 10 cm. Find the scale factor from the first figure to the second.

feedback.text: Divide the image side by its corresponding original: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.

blocks.text: Write the correspondence first, use one consistent scale factor, preserve equal angles, and check whether a length, perimeter or area needs a linear or squared factor.
Before moving on, explain the relevant property in words, show the equation or formula with units, and use the diagram markings to check that every correspondence is consistent.
